translations.text: In many parts and in many ways God formerly spoke to the fathers through the prophets; in these last days he has spoken to us through his own Son,
whom he appointed heir of all things, by whom also the ages were made.

He is the radiance of glory and the image of his power, bearing all things by the word of his power. By himself he made the purification of our sins, and he sat down at the right hand of his riches [?] in the heights.
He was as much better than the angels as the name he inherited is better than theirs.
For to which of the angels did he ever say: You are my Son, and today I have begotten you? And again he says: I will be a Father to him, and he shall be a Son to me.
And when he again brings the firstborn into the world, he says: And let all the angels of God worship him.
But of the angels he says: Who made his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire.
But of the Son he says: Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; a rod of governance is also the rod of your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness more than your companions.
And: You, Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the heavens are the works of your hands;
they shall pass away, but you remain forever; and all shall grow old like garments,
and like clothing you shall change them, and they shall be changed. But you yourself are the same, and your years shall not fail.
To which of the angels did he ever say: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies beneath your feet?
Are they not all tribute-bearing spirits, sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation?
Therefore we must take all the greater care, we who have heard these things, so that we do not grow weak.
For if the word spoken through angels proved firm, and every transgressor of the law and every disobedient person received a judgment of retribution,
how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation, which began by being spoken through the Lord and was confirmed to us by those who heard,
God bearing witness along with them by signs and wonders and various powers and by distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his will?
For it was not to angels that he subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking;
but someone has testified somewhere, saying: What is man, that you remember him? Or the son of man, that you look upon him?
You made him a little lower than your angels; with glory and honor you crowned him;
you subjected all things beneath his feet. For in subjecting all things, he left nothing that was not subject to him. But now we do not yet see all things subjected.
But we see Jesus, made a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor through that suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for all.
For it was fitting for him, for whom are all things and from whom are all things, who brought many children to glory, to make the leader of our salvation perfect through suffering.
For he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, for which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying:
I will declare your name to my brothers, and in the midst of the assembly I will sing to you.
And then he says: I will trust in him; and again he says: Behold, I and the children whom God has given me.

For he shared with the children in flesh and blood, and he himself likewise took on the same things as they, so that through death he might destroy the one who held the power of death, that is, the devil,
and might set free those who, through fear of death, were subject to affliction throughout their whole life.
For in no way did he begin from angels, but he began from the race of Abraham.
Therefore it was necessary for him to be like his brothers in all things, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest before God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
For because he himself suffered and was tested, he is able to help those who are being tested as well.
Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus Christ,
who is faithful to the one who made him, as Moses also was in all his house.
For this one was worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house.
For every house is built by someone, but the one who built all things is God.
And Moses too was faithful over all his house, as a servant, for a testimony to the things that were spoken.
But Christ was faithful as a son over his house; and we are his house, if we hold firmly to the boldness and the boast of hope until the end.
Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me; they tried me and saw my works for forty years.
Therefore I was wearied with that generation and said: They always go astray in their heart, and they have not known my ways.
As I swore in my wrath: they shall not enter my rest.
Take care, brothers, lest perhaps there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, falling away from the living God.
But comfort yourselves day by day, as long as it is still called today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin.
For we have become partakers with Christ, if we hold firmly to the beginning of our strength until the end.
When it says: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation.
For some heard and provoked him, but not all who came out of Egypt through Moses.
And with whom was he wearied for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bones fell in the wilderness?
Or to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest? Was it not to the disobedient?
And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.
Let us therefore fear, lest, while the promise of entering his rest is still left open, any of you should think himself to have fallen short.
For we too have had the good news proclaimed to us, just as they did; but the word that they heard profited them nothing, since it was not mixed with faith in those who heard.
But let us, we who believe, enter that rest, as he said: As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter my rest; and this although the works had been made from the beginning of the world.
For he has said somewhere concerning the seventh day thus: And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.
And after this he says again: They shall not enter my rest.
Since, therefore, it remains for some to enter into it, and those who earlier had the good news proclaimed to them did not enter because of unbelief,
he again appoints a certain day, speaking through David after so long a time, as has been said: Today, if we hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.
For if Joshua son of Nun had given them rest, he would not speak after this of another day.
Does a sabbath rest, then, remain for the people of God?
For whoever has entered his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his own.
Let us therefore hasten to enter that rest, so that no one may fall into the same pattern of unbelief. (6)

For the word of God is living and powerful and sharper than any two-edged sword; and it reaches as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and it is a judge of the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
And no created thing is hidden before him, but everything is naked and with neck bowed before his eyes, concerning whom this word of ours is spoken.
We have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God; let us hold fast to the confession rightly.
For we do not have such a high priest as could not have mercy on our weaknesses, but one tested in every way in like manner, without sin.
Let us therefore approach the thrones of grace openly, so that we may receive mercy and find grace in the time of help.
For every high priest, taken from among men, is appointed on behalf of men in the things relating to God, to offer offerings and sacrifices for sins with forgiveness,
and he is able to show mercy alike to the ignorant and the erring, since weakness lies upon him as well;
and because of this he must offer sacrifice for sins, as for the people, so also for himself.
And no one takes the honor by himself, but only one who is called by God, as Aaron was.
So too Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but it was he who said to him: You are my Son, and today I have begotten you.
As he also says in another place: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
As in the days of his flesh he offered entreaty and prayer with a loud voice and tears to the one able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent fear.
And though he was indeed the Son, he learned obedience from what he suffered;
And he was made perfect, and he became for all who obey him the cause of eternal life;
and he was named by God high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
Concerning him we have much to say, and it is hard to explain in speech, since you have become weak in hearing.
For indeed you ought to have been teachers by this time; yet again you need to be taught certain elements of the beginning of the words of God; and you have come to need milk and not solid food.
For everyone who takes milk is ignorant of the word of righteousness, because he is an infant.
But solid food belongs to the perfect, who by that practice have minds trained to discern good and evil.
Therefore let us leave the beginning of the words of Christ and go on to perfection; let us not again lay the foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
of the teaching of baptism and of the laying on of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead and of eternal judgment.
And this let us do, if God commands us.
For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, who have tasted the gifts of heaven and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit
and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the power of the age to come,
and who have fallen, to be renewed again to repentance, since they crucify the Son of God for themselves and expose him to shame.
For the land that drinks the rain which comes upon it many times, and brings forth green plants useful to those for whose sake it is worked, receives a blessing from God.
But if it brings forth thorns and thistles, it is worthless and close to a curse, and its end is to be burned.
But concerning you, beloved, we are confident of better things, things close to salvation, even though we speak in this way.
For there is no falsehood with God, that he should forget your works and the labor of your love, which you showed for the sake of his name, for you served the saints and are serving them still.
We desire that each one of you show the same eagerness toward the full assurance of hope until the end,
so that you may not grow sluggish, but be imitators of those who through faith and long-suffering inherited the promises. (8)
For God made a promise to Abraham, and since there was no one greater by whom he could swear, he swore by himself;
and he said: "With blessing I will bless you, and with multiplying I will multiply you."
And so he was long-suffering and obtained the promise.
For men swear by one greater than themselves, and an oath is the confirmation that ends all their dispute.
Therefore God, wishing all the more to show the heirs of the promise the immovability of his counsel, made an oath the mediator,
so that by these two immovable things, in which God was able [?] to lie, we might have strong consolation, we who have entrusted ourselves to holding fast to the hope set before us,
which we hold as an anchor of the soul, secure and firm, and entering within the inner veil,
where Jesus the forerunner entered on our behalf, having become high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham when he was returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him,
to whom Abraham gave a tenth of everything as a portion, is first translated "king of righteousness," and then "king of Salem," which is king of peace,
without father, without mother, of unrecorded lineage; he has neither beginning of days nor end of life, but he is made like the Son of God and remains a priest forever.
See then how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth from the choicest spoils.

And those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment to receive a tithe from the people according to the law, that is, from their own brothers, even those who came forth from the loins of Abraham.
But he whose lineage is not recorded among them received a tithe from Abraham, and blessed the one who had the promise.
And beyond all dispute the lesser is blessed by the greater.
And here men who die receive tithes, but there it is testified that he lives,
and, to put it briefly, on account of Abraham, Levi too, who receives the tithe, was himself offered as a tithe;
for he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him. 10

For if perfection had been through the Levitical priesthood (for on it the people were given the law), what need was there still for another priest to be raised up according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For with the change of the priesthood it is evident that, of necessity, a change of the law also takes place,
since he of whom this is said belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever stood before the altar.
It is evident beforehand that our Lord has dawned for us from the tribe of Judah, a tribe of which Moses said nothing concerning priesthood.
And it is still more evident if another high priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
who is not according to the law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an imperishable life.
For it is testified: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
For there comes about a setting aside of the former commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; but there is the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And inasmuch as it was not without an oath (for some have become priests without an oath,
but this one with an oath, through him who said to him: The Lord has sworn and will not repent: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek),
by so much has Jesus become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And some, many in number, were appointed priests, being prevented by death from remaining.
But this one, because of his remaining forever, holds that priesthood as one that does not pass away.
Therefore he is able to save completely those who draw near to God through him, and he lives forever to intercede for them.
For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sins, and higher than the heavens,
who does not need, day after day like those high priests, to offer sacrifice first for his own sins and then for the people; for he did this himself once, when he offered himself.
For the law appointed as high priests men who had weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appointed a Son made perfect forever.
Now the chief point of what has been said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the thrones of glory in the heavens,
a minister of the holy things and of the true tent, which the Lord built and not man.
For every high priest is appointed to offer sacrifice and offering; therefore it is fitting that he too should have something that he may offer for himself.
For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest, since there are priests who offer sacrifices according to the law,

who served as a figure and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses received a command concerning the making of the tent, for it says: See and make everything according to the pattern that I showed you on the mountain.
But now he has attained a better ministry, as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which has been established as law upon that better promise.
For if that first one had been blameless, no place would have been sought for the second,
for he reproaches them and says to them: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will accomplish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they did not remain in my law, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.

For this is the covenant that I made with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds, and I will write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
And no one shall teach his fellow citizen, and no one his brother, saying, "Know the Lord," for all shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest of them.
For I will be merciful toward their falsehoods, and I will remember their iniquities and their sins no more.
When he says "new," he has made the first one old; and what is becoming old and growing aged is near to destruction.
For that first law had ordinances of service and that earthly holy place;
for a first tent was prepared, in which were the lampstand and the table and the setting out of the loaves, which was called "Holy."
And after that was the second curtain of the tent, which was called "Holy of Holies."
It had a golden censer and the ark of the law, covered outside and inside with gold, in which were the golden jar full of manna, and the rod of Aaron that had sprouted, and the tablets of the law,
And above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat; of these things there is no speaking now one by one.
And when these things had been set up in this way, the priests would continually enter the first tent and carry out the service.
But into the inner one only the high priest would enter, once a year, and not without blood, which he would offer for himself and for the ignorance of the people.
And this the Holy Spirit made known: that the way of the holy places had not yet been revealed, while the first tent still held its status.
This was a parable of the time that was to come, in which sacrifices and offerings were being offered that could not make those who offered them perfect in heart,
but only concerning foods and drinks and various washings and ordinances of the flesh, until the time of the coming dispensation.
But Christ came, the high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hand, that is, not of this creation,
nor with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood he entered once into the holy place and found eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and calves and the ashes of heifers, sprinkled on those who were defiled, purified them as to the purification of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify your minds also from dead works to serve the living God!

And for this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, a death having taken place for redemption from the transgressions under the first law, those who are called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
For where there is a written will, the death of the one who wrote the will must necessarily come in,
for a written testament is valid only after people have died; otherwise it is never valid, as long as the one who wrote the testament is still alive.
Therefore not even the first one was inaugurated without blood.

For when all the commandments had been spoken according to the law by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats with water, with scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled the book itself and all the people,
and said: This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded you.
The tent itself and all the vessels of the service he likewise sprinkled with blood in the same way.
And according to the law almost everything was purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there was no forgiveness.
It is necessary, then, since the copies of the heavenly things were purified by these, that the heavenly things themselves be purified by better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter holy places made by hand, copies of the true ones, but heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God for us,
nor in order to offer himself many times, as the high priest enters the holy place once a year with the blood of another;
for then he would have had to suffer many times since the creation of the world; but now, once, at the end of the ages, he has appeared to set sins at nought by his sacrifice.
And just as it is laid up for people to die once, and after that the judgment,
So also Christ was offered once for many, to blot out sins, and the second time he will appear without sins to those who await him as Savior.

For the Law had a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities. With those sacrifices, year after year, which they offered continually, they could never bring to perfection those who offered them.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased from offering, since those who offered, once cleansed, would no longer have had any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is again a remembrance of sins year after year,
for the blood of goats and bulls cannot blot out sins.
Therefore, when he comes into the world, he says: Offering and sacrifice you did not desire, but you established a body for me.
A burnt offering for sins you did not ask.
Then I said: Behold, I come; at the head of the books it is written of me, to do your will, O my God.
Above he says: Sacrifice and offering and burnt offering, and those for sins, you did not want, nor were you pleased with them, which are offered according to the Law;
then he said: Behold, I come to do your will. He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once.
And every priest stands day after day in that service and offers the same sacrifices many times, which can never blot out sins.
But he himself offered once a sacrifice for sins forever, and he sat down at the right hand of God,
and from then on he waits until his enemies are placed under his feet.
For one sacrifice has been made perfect forever for those who are sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us, for after that saying,
namely: This is my covenant which I will promise them after those days, says the Lord: I will give my laws to their hearts, and I will write them on their minds,
and their lawless deeds and their sins I will remember no more.
But where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer need of a sacrifice for sins.
So, brothers, we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
He who renewed for us a new and living way through the veil, that is, through his flesh,
and a great high priest in the house of God:
let us draw near to him with a true heart and in fullness of faith, sprinkled in heart from an evil conscience
and washed in body with pure water. Let us hold fast the confession of hope without wavering, for he who promised me is faithful.
And let us consider one another, so as to stir one another up to love and good works.
Do not abandon your own assembly, as is the custom of some, but comfort one another, and all the more as you see this day drawing near.
For because of our willful sins, after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left any longer,
but a certain terrifying expectation of judgment, and a fury of fire that will devour those enemies.
If anyone despises the law of Moses, he dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

How much worse a punishment do you think he will be held to deserve, who tramples the Son of God underfoot, and counts as unworthy the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know him who said: "Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord." And again he says: "The Lord will judge his people."
It is a terrifying thing to fall into the hands of the living God. 15
Remember those former days, in which you were baptized and endured a great struggle of sufferings;
that is, you were made a spectacle to the world in reproaches and afflictions, and also you became sharers with those who were living in the midst of these things.
For you had compassion on my bonds, and you accepted the plundering of your possessions with joy, knowing that you have for yourselves a better treasure abiding in heaven.
Do not cast away that open confidence of yours, which has the gain of a great reward.
For you have need of patience, so that you may do the will of God and receive what was promised.
For in a little while, only a moment more, and he who is coming will come and will not delay.
But the righteous one shall live by faith; and if you withdraw from him, my soul takes no pleasure in him.
But we are not of the withdrawal that leads to destruction, but of the faith that leads to the preservation of the soul.
Now faith is the power of those who hope, the proof of things not seen.
For by this the elders received their attestation.
By faith we understand that the ages were established by the word of God, so that what is visible was made from what is not manifest.
By faith Abel offered to God more sacrifices than Cain, through which he was attested to be righteous, God bearing witness over his sacrifices; and because of this, though he died, he still speaks.
By faith Enoch was translated so that he should not see death; and he was not found, because God had translated him; for before his translation it was attested of him that he had pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible to please him; for whoever approaches God must have faith that he exists and that he becomes the giver of reward to those who seek him.

By faith Noah, having received a command concerning things not yet seen, feared and made an ark for the saving of his household, by which he condemned the world, and through that faith he became heir of righteousness.
By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and went out to the place which he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
By faith he sojourned in the land of the promise as in a foreign land, dwelling in a tent with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise;
for he was waiting for that city which has foundations, whose architect and maker is God.
By faith Sarah herself also, though she was barren, received power to conceive seed and gave birth past her time of life, for she considered him who had promised her to be faithful.
Therefore from one man, and him as good as dead, these too were born, like the stars of heaven in multitude and like the innumerable sand of the sea.
By faith all these died, and they had not yet received the promise, but they saw it from afar and greeted it and confessed that they are strangers and passers-by on the earth.
For those who say such things make it plain that they are seeking a fatherland.
And if they had been remembering that place from which they came out, they would have had time to return there.
But now their heart speaks of the better one, that is, the heavenly one; for this reason God is not at all ashamed of them, to be named their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham offered Isaac at the testing, and he who had received the promise was offering his only-begotten son,
to whom it was said: "Through Isaac shall your offspring be named for you."
He reckoned thus, that God is able even to raise from the dead, from which he also brought him back, in a figure.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and bowed in worship upon the tip of his staff.
By faith Joseph, when he was reaching his end, made mention of the going out of the sons of Israel and gave command concerning his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was fair, and they did not fear the king's command.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing rather to suffer hardship together with the people of God than to have the fleeting pleasure of sin;
he reckoned the reproach of Christ as greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking to the repayment of the reward.
By faith he left Egypt and did not fear the king's anger, for he reckoned the invisible one as though visible.
By faith he performed the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if on dry land, which the Egyptians attempted and were drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell through being encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with the disobedient, for she received the spies in peace.
And what more shall I say? For time fails me to tell of Gideon, of Barak, of Samson and of Jephthah, of David and of Samuel and of the prophets,
who by faith fought against kings: Abraham, Moses and Joshua; worked righteousness: Abraham and Phinehas; obtained promises: Joshua and Caleb; stopped the mouths of lions: David, Samson, Daniel;

quenched the power of fire: the three youths; escaped the edge of the sword: Elijah and Uriah; were made strong out of weakness: Hezekiah, Samson, Joshua; became mighty in battle: Abraham, Lot, Moses, David; routed the camps of foreigners: Joshua, Samson, Barak, Gideon, David.

Women received their dead raised: the Shunammite and the woman of Zarephath. But others ended their lives by the cutting off of their heads (it speaks of certain beheaded saints) and did not accept deliverance, so that they might be made worthy of a better resurrection; that is, the Lord thus ordained their end and did not preserve them from the sword.
But others were tried by tortures and scourging: the Maccabees and their mother; and further by chains and prisons: Jeremiah and Micaiah;

Jeremiah and Naboth had their brains dashed out with stones; Isaiah was sawn apart; Job and Zerubbabel were put to the test; Micah, Amos, and Zechariah the priest perished by death from the sword; John the Baptist, Elijah, and Elisha went about in cloaks and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, and ill-treated,
of whom this world was not worthy, wandering in the wilderness, in mountains and caves and holes of the earth, the prophets whom Obadiah fed in the wilderness.
And all these were attested through faith, and yet they did not receive what had been promised,
for God had foreseen something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect without us.

Now therefore, since we too have so great a multitude of holy martyrs surrounding us, let us put away every weight and the sin that swiftly comes upon us, and let us run with patience the contest set before us.
And let us look to Jesus, the leader and perfecter of our faith, who, in place of the joy set before him, endured the cross, despised the shame, and sat down at the right hand of the thrones of God.
Consider, then, him who endured such contradiction from sinners against himself, so that you may not grow weary in your souls and lose heart.
For you have not yet resisted to the point of blood, struggling bravely against sin,
and you have grown slack regarding the consolation that speaks to you as to sons: My son, do not be fainthearted at the discipline of the Lord, nor give way when you are reproved by him.
for the Lord disciplines those he loves, and he punishes every son whom he accepts."
If you endure discipline, God receives you as sons. For who is the son whom his father does not discipline?
But if you are far from the discipline in which all have become sharers, then you are strangers and not sons.
Now if we have had fleshly fathers and mothers as instructors, and we would revere them, shall we not much rather submit to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined for a few days according to their own will, but he does so for what is better, that they may receive of his holiness.
All discipline at the moment is not joy but sorrow; yet afterward it yields the fruit of peace to those who have been trained by it: righteousness.
Therefore lift up the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
And make straight the paths of your feet, so that the lame may not fall but rather be healed.
Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
Take care that no one falls short of the grace of God, that no root of bitterness springs up with anyone and causes trouble, and that many are not defiled by it.
Let no one be a fornicator or profane, like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
You know that after this he wanted to inherit the blessing and was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, even though he sought it with tears.
For you have not come to the mountain that can be touched by hand and that burned with fire, and to gloom and darkness and mist,
and to the sound of a trumpet and the voice of words, which those who heard it begged that no further word be added to them.
For they could not bear what was commanded: if even a beast touched the mountain, it was to be driven off with stones.
And so terrible was that spectacle that Moses said: I am terrified and trembling.
But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the myriad assembly of angels,
and to the church of the firstborn, who are enrolled in the heavens, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous who have been made perfect,
and to Jesus, the mediator of the divine covenant, and to the sprinkling with blood, which is better than what was spoken by Abel.

Take care that you do not turn away from the one who speaks. For if those who turned away from the command on earth did not escape, how much more shall we not, if we turn back from the one who is from heaven,
whose voice shook the earth then, and now he has promised, saying: Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but the heavens also.
But this "yet once more" makes known the changing of the things that are shaken, as of things made, so that what is unshaken may remain.
Therefore let us also take hold of the unshakable kingdom; we have grace, by which we serve God in a pleasing way, with fear and reverence,
for our God is a consuming fire.
Let brotherly love remain among you.
Do not forget love of strangers, for through this some, as if without knowing it, have entertained angels as guests.
Remember those in bonds, as though bound together with them, and those who are ill-treated, for you too have bodies.
Marriage is honorable in all, and the bed undefiled; but fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
Be free of the love of silver in your way of life; let what you have be enough for you, for he himself has said: I will not leave you nor forsake you.
Hence it is fitting for us to say: The Lord is my helper, I will not be afraid; what can a man do to me?
Remember your leaders, who spoke the words of God to you; look at the outcome of their life and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ yesterday and today, and he himself is the same forever.
Do not accept manifold and strange teaching, for you are well strengthened in heart by grace and not by food, from which those who walked in it gained nothing.
We have an altar from which those who serve the tent have no authority to eat.
For the animals whose blood is offered for sins in the sanctuary by the high priest, their bodies were burned outside the camp.
Therefore Jesus also, in order to sanctify the people by his own blood, suffered outside the gates.
Now therefore let us go out to him outside the camp and bear his reproach.
For we have here no city to dwell in, but we seek the one to come.
Therefore we continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips and confession of his name.
But do not forget doing good and sharing, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.
Submit to your leaders and obey them, for they keep watch over your souls, as those who will give an account, so that they may do this with joy and not with sighing, for this is not easy for you.
Pray for us also; we are confident that we have a good mind in all things and that we wish to walk rightly.
I beg you all the more to do this, so that I may come to you soon. 22
Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep by the blood of the eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
establish you in every good work to do his will, who works in us what is pleasing before him through Christ Jesus, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
But I beg you, brothers, bear with this word of entreaty, though I have written to you briefly.
You know that Timothy, our brother, is the one I have sent; with him, if he comes soon, I will see you.
Give greetings to all your leaders and to all the saints. Those who are from Italy greet you.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
